To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel promoter-binding site for the PB1 subunits in the influenza virus RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase.
we have identified a new promoter-binding site on the PB1 sub-unit of the influenza A RNA polymerase.
(i) the 233-251 region of the PB1 polymerase subunit is involved in binding to the 5' end of the viral RNA promoter and that (ii) arginine 235 is a key residue in this interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of transcription and replication of influenza A virus RNA, and the role of viral RNA polymerase in this process.
the identification of the promoter-binding site in PB1 and its functional analysis.
the mechanism of transcription of the influenza A genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 233 to 281 region of PB1 is important for vRNA promoter recognition.
PB1 has three distinct regions that are required for promoter binding, namely aa 233-249, 249-256 and 269-281.
the PB1 subunits binds the 3' vRNA promoter via a region centred on aa 249 to F254, and the 5' vRNP promoter via a region that extends from aa 233 and includes the R233, R236 and R239.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PB1 subunits binds the 3' promoter region of the viral RNA via a region that extends from aa 269 to 282.
the 233 to 256 region contains a binding site for the vRNA promoter, but the exact location and function of the 3' vRNA binding site remains to be determined.
the 5' vRNP promoter binding site in PB1 extends from amino acid residues 233 to 281, and the 3' vRNP binding site extends from 249 to 281.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3' and 5' vRNP promoter-binding regions of PB1 overlap, and that the binding of the 5' vRNAP to PB1 is not only dependent on the presence of the 3' vRNP, but that the 5' and the 3' promoter-binding sites overlap.
the 5' and the 3' vRNA promoter binding sites of PB1 are located in the N-terminal half of the protein.
the 5' vRNAPB1 promoter-binding site is not the same as the 3' vRNAPb1 promoter-binding site.
